market_context: United States; vegetable calcium content and bioavailability.
title: Vegetables Highest in Calcium

seo.title: Vegetables Highest in Calcium per 100 Grams
seo.meta_description: Collard greens, kale, bok choy, and watercress can provide meaningful calcium. Absorption matters: spinach calcium is poorly absorbed because of oxalate.
seo.search_intent: Compare calcium-rich vegetables while accounting for both content and bioavailability.

excerpt: Some leafy greens contain substantial calcium: raw collards and certain kale entries can exceed 200 mg per 100 g, bok choy is around 100 mg, and broccoli around 45–50 mg. The number alone is not enough, because spinach calcium is much less bioavailable due to oxalate.
content_html:
A calcium ranking can mislead if it only sorts the numbers in a database. What matters is both how much calcium is present and how much of it can be absorbed.

Vegetables with meaningful amounts

Raw vegetableApprox. calcium/100 g
Collard greens~230 mg
Kale, depending on type~150–250 mg
Watercress~120 mg
Bok choy~100 mg
Spinach~100 mg
Broccoli~47 mg

Variety and cooking state change the exact values.

Why spinach is the classic trap

Spinach looks competitive on total calcium but is also high in oxalate, which binds calcium and sharply reduces absorption. Calcium from low-oxalate greens such as bok choy, kale, and broccoli is generally much more available.

Cooking changes per-100-g numbers

Leafy greens collapse and lose water during cooking, so 100 g cooked can represent far more plant material than 100 g raw. Serving-size comparisons are therefore important too.

Vegetables do not have to carry the whole calcium load

Fortified plant beverages, dairy foods, calcium-set tofu, canned fish with bones, and other foods can contribute depending on the diet.

For useful plant calcium, low-oxalate greens often outperform spinach even when the raw database numbers look similar.

faq.question: Which vegetables are highest in calcium?
faq.answer: Collard greens and some types of kale are among the highest common vegetables, often above 150–200 mg per 100 g.

faq.question: Is spinach a good calcium source?
faq.answer: It contains calcium, but high oxalate makes much of it poorly absorbed.

faq.question: Does broccoli have much calcium?
faq.answer: It has less total calcium than many leafy greens, around 45–50 mg per 100 g, but the calcium is relatively bioavailable.
